messages:
Alex: Proposal: shift token attribution calculation earlier in the ingest path (pre-ledger). Rationale: consumers get deterministic attribution keys and we can emit compact proof manifests for every segment. Quick opinions?

Priya: Sounds good for downstream stability. Main concerns: duplicate suppression across retries and how we prove counts to finance without forcing raw retention forever.

Mateo: For proofs we could emit a per-kafka-segment manifest that includes a checksum and a small Merkle root over canonical records. Sign the manifest with ingest key. Finance can validate manifests + sampled rehydration.

Chen: How do we collapse duplicates? If attribution runs pre-ledger we need a stable id. Suggest fingerprint = sha256(tenant+request_id+normalized_prompt+model_hash). Keep a short dedupe window (configurable per-tenant).

Alex: Agreed. Dedupe + idempotency window will be metadata on ledger entries. Downstreams will trust ledger as source-of-truth for billing reads.

Sahana: Compliance: storing normalized prompts even briefly may expose PII. We need a redaction plan and TTLs. I'll coordinate with legal on minimum retention constraints.

Mateo: Rehydration plan: keep raw for 72 hours by default; customers can opt-in for longer windows. Most audit queries are within a week so short retention reduces storage. Manifests allow verification without always rehydrating full raw.

Chen: Backpressure/backfill: if the attribution service falls behind we must not block the ingest hot path. Suggest async attribution with optimistic ledger write that marks "attribution_pending" flag. A background reconciler fills missing attribution and emits correction manifests.

Priya: Correction manifests sound fine, but we must ensure consumers don't count pending entries. Maybe ledger stores a compact status enum: PENDING | CONFIRMED | CORRECTED. Billing reads only include CONFIRMED unless in an explicit audit mode.

Alex: Good point. We'll add status. Also need to version attribution rules; include attribution_rules_version in the canonical payload so audits can re-evaluate with historical rules if needed.

Mateo: Example manifest (compact):
```json
{
  "segment":"kafka-usage-5-0000123",
  "count":125421,
  "tokens_sum":3489123,
  "merkle_root":"sha256:deadbeef...",
  "signed_by":"ingest-key-v2",
  "schema":"manifest.v1"
}
```

Chen: Nice. Implementation details: write manifests after flush boundary, persist manifest to object storage + index to ledger for quick lookup. Signatures verified by finance service via public key.

Priya: Migration plan? We can't break existing consumers.

Alex: Phased approach: 1) start computing fingerprints & attribution in a sidecar and write manifests (no consumer changes). 2) Enable dual-write ledger entries with attribution_metadata (two weeks). 3) Flip read path for billing to prefer ledger attribution when CONFIRMED. 4) Run reconciliation job to ensure parity and deprecate legacy fields after quiet window.

Sahana: Add an explicit privacy review before step 2. Also expose per-tenant opt-outs in Console.

Priya: What about schema evolution for canonical record? We must include schema_id and a small client library to read old formats.

Chen: We'll include schema_id and a stable minimal canonical shape: {tenant, fingerprint, tokens, model, attribution_rules_version, status, provenance_ref}. Readers can use the shim lib for compatibility.

Alex: Operational metrics: surface dedupe rate, pending attribution lag, manifest publish latency, manifest verification failures. These will be SLOs for the new service.

Mateo: Cost/benefit: extra CPU at ingest, slightly more storage for short raw retention + manifests. But reduces downstream ambiguity and audit pain. Estimate +8% compute, +12% short-term storage.

Priya: One more: what about tenant-specific dedupe windows to handle replays in customer infra? Keep window configurable per tenant in their billing profile.

Chen: Yep. We'll add tenant-level config plus global sane defaults.

AuditBot: scheduled job created: ingest-manifests-monitoring at 2026-03-28T05:00Z.

Alex: Next action: I'll draft RFC with proto defs for canonical record + manifest + migration steps. Mateo, Chen — can you sketch the manifest signing flow? Sahana will coordinate compliance.

Mateo: On it.

Chen: I'll draft the shim library README and sample consumer patches.

Priya: Great, please link the RFC here when ready.

Alex: Thanks everyone — will post RFC by EOD.
